classification.difficultyReason: Find lowest common multiples of sets containing two, three or four numbers, including sets requiring extended multiple lists.

content.prompt: Find the LCMs of the following sets of numbers.

answer.worked:
Non-zero multiples of $8$: $8,16,24,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $6$: $6,12,18,24,\ldots$

The first common multiple is $24$, so the LCM is $24$.

Non-zero multiples of $10$: $10,20,30,40,50,60,70,80,90,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $18$: $18,36,54,72,90,\ldots$

The first common multiple is $90$, so the LCM is $90$.

Non-zero multiples of $16$: $16,32,48,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $24$: $24,48,\ldots$

The first common multiple is $48$, so the LCM is $48$.

Non-zero multiples of $60$: $60,120,180,240,300,360,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $72$: $72,144,216,288,360,\ldots$

The first common multiple is $360$, so the LCM is $360$.

Non-zero multiples of $6$: $6,12,18,24,30,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $10$: $10,20,30,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $15$: $15,30,\ldots$

The first multiple common to all three lists is $30$, so the LCM is $30$.

The common multiples of $10$ and $12$ begin $60,120,180,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $18$: $18,36,54,72,90,108,126,144,162,180,\ldots$

The first multiple common to all three numbers is $180$, so the LCM is $180$.

answer.short:
$540$

Compare the common multiples of $36$ and $45$ with the multiples of $27$.
answer.worked:
Non-zero multiples of $36$ begin $36,72,108,144,180,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $45$ begin $45,90,135,180,\ldots$

Their common multiples begin $180,360,540,\ldots$

Of these, $180$ and $360$ are not multiples of $27$, but $540=27\times20$.

The LCM is $540$.

answer.short:
$1020$

Every multiple of $60$ is a multiple of $12$; compare multiples of $60$ and $102$.
answer.worked:
Every multiple of $60$ is a multiple of $12$, since $60=12\times5$.

Non-zero multiples of $102$: $102,204,306,408,510,612,714,816,918,1020,\ldots$

The first number in this list that is also a multiple of $60$ is $1020=60\times17$.

The LCM is $1020$.

answer.short:
$600$

Compare the common multiples of $30$ and $40$ with the multiples of $50$ and $75$.
answer.worked:
Non-zero multiples of $30$ begin $30,60,90,120,\ldots$

Non-zero multiples of $40$ begin $40,80,120,\ldots$

Their common multiples begin $120,240,360,480,600,\ldots$

The first of these divisible by $50$ is $600$.

Also, $600=75\times8$, so it is a multiple of $75$.

The LCM is $600$.
